feat(core+cli+mcp): flyway_status — second working tool

First read-only tool, first consumer of the signed identity. Inspects
local on-disk state and reports:

  identity     reads .well-known/did.json + flyway/entity-statement.json,
               verifies the entity statement signature against the DID
               document, surfaces issues (missing files, DID mismatch,
               tampered statement, unsigned legacy statement)
  peers        reports presence of flyway/peers.yaml (no parsing yet)
  agreements   counts *.yaml files in flyway/agreements/ and lists ids

Signals (inbox/outbox) deliberately deferred — their on-disk
convention is unsettled and will land with flyway_propose / flyway_check.

CLI: `flyway status` (human output) and `flyway status --json`.
MCP: handler accepts an optional cwd argument; defaults to process.cwd().

Tests: 113 passing across the workspace (+11 status + 2 MCP).
End-to-end verified: init → status reports signatureValid=true.

feat(core): signing milestone — Signer interface + local Ed25519 default

Implements ADR-0007's signing seam. Three new pieces in flyway-core:

  signing.ts
    - canonicalize() — JCS-style deterministic JSON (sorted keys, no
      whitespace, drops undefined)
    - domainSeparated() — prefixes canonical bytes with a flyway domain
      tag so signatures cannot be replayed across artifact kinds (or
      mistaken for non-flyway signatures when keys are reused)
    - Signer interface — pluggable, async; future Cardano / HSM / KMS
      signers drop in without changing artifact-producing code
    - localEd25519Signer() — the default; wraps Node crypto.sign
    - signArtifactInline() — attaches a SignatureEnvelope to the
      artifact (W3C VC / jws-2020 inline convention)
    - verifyInlineSignedArtifact() — verifies against a DID document
    - DOMAIN_* constants for each signed artifact kind

  anchoring.ts
    - Anchor interface + AnchorReceipt type. No implementation in
      v0.1; the interface lands now so future Cardano anchors drop
      in cleanly (ADR-0007).

  init.ts
    - flywayInit() is now async; the produced entity statement carries
      an EdDSA signature over its canonical bytes
    - EntityStatement gains an optional signature field
      (SignedEntityStatement narrows it to required)

Consumers updated to await: MCP handlers, CLI runInit, CLI bin.

Tests: 104 passing across the workspace (+17 signing + 3 signature
round-trips in init + MCP + CLI).

End-to-end verified: `flyway init` writes a signed entity statement
that round-trips through verifyInlineSignedArtifact against the
generated DID document.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: accept ADR-0007 (pluggable signers and on-chain anchoring)

Decides the architectural shape of signing before signing actually
lands in flyway-core. Three separable concerns — signing (required,
default = local Ed25519), anchoring (optional, no default),
credentialing (optional, declarative). Each is its own interface;
chain-specific implementations ship as separate optional packages.

The lucky Ed25519 alignment with Cardano is named explicitly so the
integration is additive, not a refactor. flyway-core stays
chain-agnostic; @murmurations-ai/flyway-cardano and
@murmurations-ai/flyway-andamio are future optional packages, not
v0.1 blockers.

docs(architecture): how-flyway-works.html — visual companion

Hand-crafted single-file HTML reference with custom SVG diagrams:
mental model (three layers), component poster, flyway_init sequence,
cross-murmuration consent sequence, four state machines, and the
contracts tables. Tied to SHA eec423c / protocol v0.1.0.

Tufte-meets-technical-spec aesthetic: warm paper for prose, deep-blue
canvas for diagrams, amber for implemented surface, slate for deferred.
Self-contained — no build step, web fonts via Google Fonts CDN. Prints
as one cohesive document.

README updated to point readers at the visual companion alongside the
existing markdown version.
